title: Annotatio V §.X close: Beza reductio — faith-presence not empty; Tractat Germ. §.XV — stop before §.XI
pass_a_gloss: Unless perhaps he who confesses this empties the Holy Supper; or Christ’s body cannot be present by faith, though the whole Christ dwells in our hearts by faith; or presence of the body by faith is mere imagination and empty fiction (as the Author’s pen, perhaps outrunning his mind, all but blasphemes) and consequently faith itself is mere Imagination and empty Fiction; or finally he who by faith sets Christ’s flesh most present himself denies that Christ’s body, as object of faith, is present in the Supper even before faith is exerted, and as present is offered and exhibited to faith. See my German Tractate §. XV. p. 64.
pass_b_english: Unless confessing presence by faith empties the Supper; or Christ’s body cannot be present by faith though the whole Christ dwells in our hearts by faith; or faith-presence is empty imagination (the Author’s pen nearly blaspheming) so that faith itself becomes empty fiction.

Or unless he who sets Christ’s flesh most present by faith denies the body is already present in the Supper as faith’s object before faith is exerted, and as present is offered to faith — see German Tractate §.XV p.64. Stop §.X before §.XI.
source_text: Nisi fortè qui hoc fatetur, Cœnam S. evacuèt; aut non possit Christi corpus per fidem præsens esse, cùm tamen totus Christus per fidem in cordibus nostris habitet; aut præsentia corporis per fidem, sit merè imaginaria & inane commentum (uti calamus Autoris mentem fortè ejus præcurrens, tantum non blasphemat) perque consequens, fides mera Imaginatio & inane Commentum sit; aut denique, qui per fidem, carnem Christi præsentissimam statuit, hic ipse neget, corpus Christi, ceu objectum fidei, in Cœna, etiam jam ante fidem exsertam, in eadem præsens esse, atque prout præsens est, fidei offerri ac exhiberi. Vid. Tractat. meum Germ. §. XV. pag. 64.
